facts.statement: Europatitan remains were first discovered in 2003 at the El Oterillo II locality in the Castrillo de la Reina Formation of Burgos, Spain.
facts.quote: Sauropod remains were first found at a locality called El Oterillo II, which is part of the Castrillo de la Reina Formation in the province of Burgos in Spain in 2003.

facts.statement: The genus Europatitan was formally described in 2017 by a team led by Fidel Torcida Fernández-Baldor and colleagues.
facts.quote: Finally, in 2017, the specimen received a full description by the authors Fidel Torcida Fernández-Baldor, José Ignacio Canudo, Pedro Huerta, Miguel Moreno-Azanza, and Diego Montero.

facts.statement: The genus Europatitan contains only one known species, Europatitan eastwoodi.
facts.quote: It contains a single species: the type species, Europatitan eastwoodi.

facts.statement: Europatitan lived during the Early Cretaceous, approximately 125 million years ago, in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: Europatitan eastwoodi es la única especie conocida del género extinto Europatitan, un dinosaurio saurópodo sonfospóndilo que vivió a mediados del Cretácico entre finales del Barremiense a principios del Aptiense, hace 125 millones de años en lo que es hoy Europa.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen includes numerous vertebrae, ribs, shoulder and hip bones, and a single tooth.
facts.quote: Fernández-Baldor and colleagues listed the following elements as belonging to the holotype: five cervical vertebrae, one dorsal vertebra, nine caudal vertebrae, 11 cervical ribs, five dorsal ribs, seven chevrons, both scapulae, the left coracoid, two left metacarpals, both pubis bones, both ischia, and a single tooth.

facts.statement: Europatitan is distinguished by unique features such as a crest on the front of its dorsal ribs and rugose surfaces on its scapula.
facts.quote: The autapomorphies include: a crest on the front surface of the dorsal ribs, two rugose surfaces on the deltoid crest of the scapula, triradiate laminae on the parapophysis of the cervical vertebrae, and numerous other features of the vertebrae.

facts.statement: Researchers estimate that Europatitan could have reached a total length of 27 meters and a weight of 35 tons.
facts.quote: Los autores de la investigación también han estimado que sería uno de los más grandes en Europa: la longitud total sería de 27 metros, y su peso llegaría a las 35 toneladas.

facts.statement: If its neck was held vertically, Europatitan's head could have been positioned up to 16 meters above the ground, making it one of the tallest known dinosaurs in Europe.
facts.quote: Si esta posibilidad es correcta, la cabeza de Europatitan podría situarse a unos 16 metros por encima del suelo, de modo que este uno de los dinosaurios conocidos más altos de Europa.

facts.statement: Europatitan is generally classified as a member of Titanosauriformes and is sometimes placed within Somphospondyli.
facts.quote: It is generally agreed to be a member of Titanosauriformes, and is sometimes considered to be a member of Somphospondyli.

facts.statement: Other analyses have corroborated a close evolutionary relationship between Europatitan and the genus Tastavinsaurus.
facts.quote: However, a close relationship to Tastavinsaurus has been corroborated by other analyses.

facts.statement: The presence of Europatitan in Europe may reflect an exchange of vertebrate faunas between Gondwana and Laurasia at the beginning of the Cretaceous.
facts.quote: El origen de estos dinosaurios se relacionaría con un proceso de intercambio de faunas de vertebrados que habría ocurrido al comienzo del Cretácico entre Gondwana y Laurasia.
